title: 精确到毫米的胡萝卜  (Carrots by the Millimetre)

segments.t: By ten o'clock Wednesday morning, bread loaves are golden in the oven and Hao stands at the chopping board beside Mei and Peng with a neat row of carrots and onions. Listen first.
小美，快看志豪的菜板——每一颗胡萝卜丁都一模一样！
哥，大小一样的菜丁熟得一样快。这是基本物理！
志鹏，尽管笑吧，这是我厨房里见过最整齐的备菜！
锅里的橄榄油热了——洋葱和胡萝卜现在下锅吗？
对！炒三分钟炒出甜味，再加红扁豆和热高汤。
主厨，接下来要放院子里的百里香和欧芹吗？
用细绳绑两小枝新鲜香草，最后再放一小撮盐。
在石头厨房里听热汤慢慢咕嘟，比城里堵车强多了！
真有意思——三年前我们在电话里吵架，今天却一起煮汤。
哥，提醒我以后再也别等三年才给你打电话了。
好啦，两兄弟，先别掉眼泪——我的面包计时器响了！
戴上烤箱手套！八个脆皮面包热腾腾出炉啦！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
小美，快看志豪的菜板——每一颗胡萝卜丁都一模一样！
'Look at Hao's cutting board, Mei—every single carrot cube is identical!' Peng ends with a classic four-word idiom meaning "cast from the very same mould", Mandarin's vivid way to say "identical".
哥，大小一样的菜丁熟得一样快。这是基本物理！

'Cubes of the same size cook at the exact same speed, brother. Basic physics!' Mandarin builds the word for "size" by gluing two opposites together: "big-small". And Hao calls Peng warmly by the single syllable for "older brother".
志鹏，尽管笑吧，这是我厨房里见过最整齐的备菜！
'Laugh all you want, Peng—that is the neatest soup prep my kitchen has ever seen!' "Prep work" in a Chinese kitchen is a compact two-character chunk literally meaning "prepare-dishes".
锅里的橄榄油热了——洋葱和胡萝卜现在下锅吗？
'The olive oil in the pot is warm—do the onions and carrots go in now?' Home cooks use the crisp two-word expression "go-down-pot" whenever chopped ingredients hit hot oil or boiling water.
对！炒三分钟炒出甜味，再加红扁豆和热高汤。

'Yes! Stir three minutes to bring out the sweetness, then add red lentils and hot broth.' Repeating the cooking action—"stir three minutes, stir-out sweetness"—gives both the timing and the goal in one smooth breath.
主厨，接下来要放院子里的百里香和欧芹吗？
'Do we add the courtyard thyme and parsley next, chef?' Thyme has a poetic Chinese name: "hundred-mile fragrance", because a tiny sprig scents the whole room.
用细绳绑两小枝新鲜香草，最后再放一小撮盐。
'Tie two fresh herb sprigs with string, and add one tiny pinch of salt at the end.' Mandarin has a dedicated counter for "a pinch" that pictures gathering a few grains between three fingertips.
在石头厨房里听热汤慢慢咕嘟，比城里堵车强多了！
'Listening to hot soup simmer gently in a stone kitchen beats city traffic any day!' Hao uses a cosy sound word—"gu-du"—that imitates thick soup quietly bubbling in a pot.
真有意思——三年前我们在电话里吵架，今天却一起煮汤。

'Funny—three years ago we argued on the phone, and today we make soup together.' That little contrast word right after "today" quietly underscores how far the two brothers have come—like English "and yet".
哥，提醒我以后再也别等三年才给你打电话了。

'Remind me never to wait three years before calling you again, brother.' The tiny word before "phone you" signals that three years was far too long a wait, carrying all of Hao's warmth in one syllable.
好啦，两兄弟，先别掉眼泪——我的面包计时器响了！
'All right, brothers, save the tears—my bread timer is ringing!' Mei breaks the tender moment with a grin, literally saying "don't drop eye-tears yet" as her oven timer goes off.
戴上烤箱手套！八个脆皮面包热腾腾出炉啦！
'Oven mitts on! Eight crusty loaves coming out of the oven piping hot!' "Fresh out of the oven" is a punchy two-character word—"exit-oven"—also used in Mandarin for brand-new songs or exam results.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
小美，快看志豪的菜板——每一颗胡萝卜丁都一模一样！
哥，大小一样的菜丁熟得一样快。这是基本物理！
志鹏，尽管笑吧，这是我厨房里见过最整齐的备菜！
锅里的橄榄油热了——洋葱和胡萝卜现在下锅吗？
对！炒三分钟炒出甜味，再加红扁豆和热高汤。
主厨，接下来要放院子里的百里香和欧芹吗？
用细绳绑两小枝新鲜香草，最后再放一小撮盐。
在石头厨房里听热汤慢慢咕嘟，比城里堵车强多了！
真有意思——三年前我们在电话里吵架，今天却一起煮汤。
哥，提醒我以后再也别等三年才给你打电话了。
好啦，两兄弟，先别掉眼泪——我的面包计时器响了！
戴上烤箱手套！八个脆皮面包热腾腾出炉啦！
Golden loaves come out of the oven and fragrant lentil soup simmers on the stove as the two brothers work side by side. See you next time.
再见！
